label: September 1918
headline: The Line Breaks
deck: Americans take St Mihiel; the Allies storm the Hindenburg Line from the Meuse to the sea
caption: American infantry go forward through the shattered woods of the Argonne
body: On 12 September the First American Army under General Pershing attacks the St Mihiel salient with French troops at its side, and in two days the salient is gone. A fortnight later the Allied armies strike together from the Argonne to Flanders. On 29 September British troops cross the St Quentin Canal and break the Hindenburg Line.

In the Balkans the Allied army from Salonika breaks the Bulgarian front, and Bulgaria signs an armistice on 29 September. In Palestine the Turkish armies are routed at Megiddo, and Allenby's horsemen ride for Damascus.

In Flanders the Belgian army and the British take Houthulst Forest, Passchendaele and Dixmude in two days. At Spa Ludendorff tells the Kaiser that the army can hold no longer: Germany must ask for an armistice.
briefs: The second wave of the Spanish influenza reaches the army camps of Massachusetts
Eugene Debs is sentenced to ten years for speaking against the war
